# mapsforge-poi

**Mapsforge points-of-interest files of your regions, for searching on a phone**

- **Version recorded:** station
- **Categories:** `navigation-maps`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/mapsforge/mapsforge>
- **Needs first:** `osm-regions`, `osmosis`, `libmapsforge-java`

## What it does

Builds one Mapsforge `.poi` file per region `osm-regions` downloaded: a small SQLite database of the region's points of interest, chosen by the writer's own default tag mapping, that a phone map app searches offline beside a Mapsforge map. It runs as the operator in a staging directory. The files land under /usr/local/share/hammunition/data/mapsforge-poi/, and `hammunition maps phone` gathers them.

## Why you would want it

A map shows where things are; a POI file lets the phone find them by name or kind with no network. Built on the laptop from the same regions as the map, so the two match. By their own documentation, Cruiser, Locus Map, OruxMaps and c:geo read Mapsforge POI files; none has been checked on a phone here.

## Before it will work

`osm-regions` with at least one region set in station config, and the archive's `osmosis` and `libmapsforge-java`; all install first. The POI writer is downloaded once from Maven Central (18.8 MB) and checked against the sha256 above. With no regions set this unit is deferred by name.

## How it installs

- converted from osm-regions by mapsforge-poi (ODbL-1.0, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), running `mapsforge-poi-writer-0.25.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar` fetched from https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/mapsforge/mapsforge-poi-writer/0.25.0/mapsforge-poi-writer-0.25.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar (18827962 bytes, LGPL-3.0), sha256 `85dd23488511f51a710139dffc8c622d184ea93e817c4ec27dde1c222b7432a7`, pinned by Hammunition; a signature is published at https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/mapsforge/mapsforge-poi-writer/0.25.0/mapsforge-poi-writer-0.25.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar.asc and not verified

## Known problems

Measured on one region, Delaware (22 MB download), on 2026-09-29: 23 s, 0.47 GB of memory, a POI file 0.21 times the download holding 22,785 points, and under half the download written to disk while it runs. The plan uses 0.21 and 0.5 and says they were measured on one region. The writer is not packaged by any archive, so it is the one file here pinned by Hammunition rather than signed by a distribution; its .asc signature is recorded and not verified. It unpacks sqlite-jdbc's native library at run time, into the staging directory, not /tmp. Not loaded on a phone yet. The file carries the Open Database License obligations of the data.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- Follows osm-regions: a region whose downloaded file changed is built again on the next install. The writer is pinned to one release; a new mapsforge release (https://github.com/mapsforge/mapsforge/releases) is a manifest change: download it once, hash it, compare with Central's .sha256, and bump the url, sha256 and size together. Every POI file is then built again, because its record names the writer's digest.

## Where to get help with the software itself

GitHub issues at https://github.com/mapsforge/mapsforge/issues; the POI writer's options are documented in the repository's docs directory.
